{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony asked to think through the mechanics of using git to capture epoch and increment snapshots; these are the options and their costs, not a settlement.

THE TENSION THAT ORGANISES EVERYTHING: git can only store the past. A commit is something that happened. A planned epoch is a claim about a future that has not happened, so there is nothing for git to hold unless someone AUTHORS a speculative design and commits it.

(a) EPOCH BRANCHES — Anthony's original idea, 2026-07-28: "epoch branches: project_x:epoch_1 captures what we expect the graph to look like at epoch_1." A branch is a real place to work: you can draft a future design there, run the detectors on it, and diff it against main with machinery that already exists.
    Costs, recorded beside it rather than against it: a branch is a MOVING POINTER and a plan is a DATED CLAIM — when the plan changes the branch moves, and nothing records that it moved, which is exactly what `req:plans-move-honestly` needs. A speculative full export also restates the entire design to express a delta about a handful of requirements, so it is expensive to author and stale on the next merge to main. And N repos times M epochs is N times M branches, each drifting independently.

(b) PLANS LIVE ONLY IN THE GRAPH. A planned epoch is a node plus scheduled edges — no git object at all, because there is no past to point at. "What does the design look like at epoch 3" becomes a COMPUTED view (today's design plus what is scheduled to be satisfied by then) rather than a stored artifact.
    Cost: you cannot open a future design in an editor or run a detector over it as a whole; you get a projection, not a document.

(c) BOTH, SCOPED DIFFERENTLY — the shape the costs seem to point at. Branches are a fine WORKSPACE for exploring a future architecture and a poor RECORD of a plan. The record lives in the graph as a dated, versioned claim; a branch is somewhere to prototype one when a person wants to see it whole.

WORTH KNOWING BEFORE DECIDING: the forward half of the CAPABILITY view already exists in the vocabulary. `Release.status` is `planned | built | deployed | retired`, so a planned increment is expressible today. The forward half of the TIME view does not: `DesignEpoch.epoch_type` is `baseline | revision | milestone | incident_response | release_cut` with no value meaning "this has not happened yet". That asymmetry is real and is the smallest concrete gap found while thinking this through.","name":"OPEN — does a planned epoch live in git, or only in the graph?","rationale":"Anthony's idea and Anthony's question; recorded so the reasoning survives whichever way it goes. The framing "two paired views of the same architecture" and the epoch-branch mechanism are both his (2026-07-28), as is the request to work out the git mechanics (2026-07-30).

Not argued down: option (a) is recorded with its virtue stated first, because a branch genuinely is the only place you can look at a future design as a whole, and that is not nothing.","status":"proposed"}
